newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Canberra says no to Telstra preference shares.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Canberra says no to Telstra preference shares.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday that Independent senator Brian Harradine's proposal to issue redeemable preference shares in communications carrier Telstra Corp held no attraction.
"This holds no attraction for the government," Costello told parliament.
"It essentially amounts to a financing transaction," he said.
"It essentially would be borrowing off back of the Telstra security and if the government is to borrow it would prefer to borrow on its own account with its own credit rating."

The government needs the vote of Harradine and another Independent for parliamentary passage of the Telstra (Dilution of Public Ownership) Bill, which would authorise a one-third privatisation of the telecoms carrier by simple sale of shares.
Harradine has said that he would not back the bill in its present form.
The bill has passed the government-dominated House of Representatives. The Senate is expected to vote on it next month.
The government expects the sale would raise about A$8 billion.
